title: Antiretroviral Therapy in Children and Adolescents Living with HIV

blocks.text: Antiretroviral Therapy in Children and Adolescents Living with HIV
Maximally and durably suppress plasma HIV RNA (to <50 copies/ml)
Reduce HIV-associated morbidity and prolong the duration and quality of survival.

ART in children has been proven to increase survival and decrease HIV-related morbidity and mortality. Children should be started on ART as soon they are diagnosed including those who are presumably diagnosed.

Treat all of them regardless of WHO clinical stage or CD4 cell count
Children below 18months old who qualify for presumptive diagnosis
Start ART while waiting for DNA-PCR confirmation test results.

Table 6.14: First-Line ARV Regimens in Infants and Children under 15 years
TAF is contraindicated in TB/HIV co-infection as Rifampicin lowers TAF concentration below the therapeutic level.
Consider PI based ARV regimen if unable to use DTG and EFV
When a child is taking a Rifampicin-based TB regimen, the DTG dose should be administered 12 hourly to reach therapeutic levels.
*TDF/3TC/EFV (TLE400) should only be used in cases of DTG intolerance as NNRTI associated transmitted drug resistance is reported to be above the recommended threshold (≥10%) for not using NNRTIs.

Children on Anti TB and TB preventive treatment (3HR) should receive an addition of pDTG with a dosage according to body weight
TDF is only approved for children above 12 years with weight ≥ 30 kg because of TDF-associated reduction in bone density
DTG 50mg is recommended for children with weight ≥ 20 kgs
Neonate should be given ART as per table 6.15b above until they reach 4 weeks of age and 3 kg then transition to pALD
pALD is not recommended for children below 3kg and for those with below 3kg, provide ABC/3TC 120/60mg (double scored) plus DTG 10mg (single scored)
